key_insight: Fusing camera images with IMU signals via a lightweight bidirectional cross-attention and an adaptive gating layer yields more robust road surface classification that generalizes across diverse environmental and operational conditions.
problem_solved: Existing RSC models fail to generalize because datasets and models use limited sensing modalities and lack environmental diversity; this work provides a multimodal framework and dataset to close that gap.
method: Curate a new, diverse multimodal dataset pairing synchronized images and inertial measurements across varied surfaces, lighting, and weather.
Fuse visual and IMU streams with a lightweight bidirectional cross-attention module to enable rich cross-modal interactions.
Apply an adaptive gating layer to selectively weight modality contributions for robust classification under changing conditions.
impact: Practitioners get a practical sensor-fusion approach and a richer dataset that improve RSC robustness and deployment reliability for predictive maintenance, ADAS, and autonomous systems.

paper_title: A New Dataset and Framework for Robust Road Surface Classification via Camera-IMU Fusion
paper_authors: Willams de Lima Costa, Thifany Ketuli Silva de Souza, Jonas Ferreira Silva, Carlos Gabriel Bezerra Pereira, Bruno Reis Vila Nova
